title: Business Analyst II
description: Business Analyst II Are you a strategic planner and problem-solver? Are you looking to develop your Data Analyst career? About the Team: Mercury is RX’s global registration and eCommerce platform, supporting the journeys that bring visitors and exhibitors into our events. Its capabilities span registration, purchasing, badging and onsite access, connecting customer experiences with the data and business systems behind them. We work across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Product Success and regional business teams to deliver reliable services, improve customer experiences and create measurable business value. About the Role We’re seeking a Business Analyst with a strong focus on User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to bridge product delivery and business validation. You’ll coordinate testing, help business users evaluate new features, manage feedback, and communicate releases in clear, accessible language. The focus is hands-on business acceptance and coordination—not software development or test automation engineering. Responsibilities (What you’ll do) Plan and coordinate business acceptance testing Partner with Product Managers, Product Owners, and Business Analysts to understand desired outcomes, user journeys, business rules, and acceptance criteria. Turn requirements into practical, risk-based UAT scenarios covering standard journeys, exceptions, and relevant regional variations. Coordinate testing scope and schedules, providing participants with clear instructions, test-event links, and prerequisites. Work with engineering, QA, and configuration teams to ensure environments, test data, and configurations are ready before testing. Perform hands-on business validation and help users investigate and reproduce unexpected results. Manage feedback, defects, and acceptance evidence Maintain a consolidated record of business feedback and communicate test completion, outstanding observations, and potential enhancements. Separate defects from configuration issues, clarification requests, and enhancement ideas, working with product and technical teams to agree next steps. Document reproducible issues, including expected and actual results, supporting evidence, and business impact, and coordinate retesting after fixes. Report progress, coverage, blockers, and residual risks so decision-makers can clearly assess readiness. Coordinate acceptance evidence and follow-up while keeping approval and validation accountability with the relevant Business Units. Support release communication and continuous improvement Prepare business-facing release updates that explain what changed, why it matters, and any relevant limitations or actions. Keep testing guidance, feedback records, and supporting documentation accessible to global stakeholders. Create reusable scenarios and checklists to improve consistency and reduce repeated effort across releases. Apply lessons from UAT and production issues to strengthen future acceptance coverage and identify gaps earlier. Collaborate across regions and time zones, keeping dependencies, decisions, and ownership clear. Requirements (What you’ll bring) Practical experience in UAT, business analysis, functional testing, or a similar role supporting user-facing digital products. Experience translating requirements and business processes into clear acceptance criteria and end-to-end test scenarios. Ability to organize testing with business users, balance competing priorities, and follow issues through to documented outcomes. Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to explain business impact as well as technical symptoms. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing user guidance, test summaries, and release updates. Experience with issue-tracking and collaborative documentation tools such as Jira and Confluence, or equivalents. Understanding of Agile delivery and the differences between engineering QA, business acceptance, and release approval. A collaborative approach and confidence working with technical and non-technical stakeholders in a distributed team. Useful, but not essential, skills Experience with event registration, ticketing, eCommerce, or other transaction-based customer journeys. Familiarity with payments, invoicing, discounts, upgrades, entitlements, or integrations between customer-facing and back-office systems. Exposure to onsite operational tools, badge management, or access-control workflows. Awareness of accessibility, localization, and data-quality considerations in business acceptance testing. Experience with test-management tools, basic data queries, or API-testing tools to support investigations. What success looks like Business users know what to test, how to participate, and where to provide feedback. Critical business journeys have clear acceptance coverage and traceable results. Defects and feedback are actionable, assigned, and followed through, with unresolved risks visible before release decisions. Business approvers receive concise evidence to support acceptance decisions. Release communications clearly explain changes and limitations, helping teams prepare for adoption. Reusable guidance and lessons learned make each testing cycle more effective. Why join us? Help shape digital experiences that connect online registration with the live event experience. You’ll work across product, technology, and business operations, building domain knowledge while improving how changes are validated and communicated. RX values collaboration, inclusion, curiosity, and learning, with opportunities to contribute across a global network. Work in a Way That Works for You We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organization. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous well-being initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals. title: QA Analyst - Intern
description: Job Description: Intern: QA Analyst About Us: UpEnergy is the leading developer of anti-poverty climate impact projects in Africa. We accelerate decarbonization and while delivering long-term health and income benefits in local communities. We provide life-improving clean technologies and carbon reduction and capture projects that protect the local environment, deliver health benefits and cleaner air, and reduce poverty through financial savings and employment. Our project sustainably benefits and enables people to live better lives within more climate resilient communities. To date, UpEnergy has built over 95 emission reduction projects, impacted over 4 million lives, and reduced over 3 million tons of CO2 Emissions across 10 countries. All UpEnergy’s work is characterized by respect for the people we serve, rigorous measurement, deep local knowledge and established teams on the ground to ensure the highest impact and results. We do all this through our commitment to drive long-term business growth through technical innovation, close customer engagement and increased data-driven decision making. The UpEnergy team continues to grow, across multiple African countries, from 20 to over 170+ full time team members in the past two years, reflecting the growth of the company for which we now seek incredible, like-minded talent who are excited to join us in delivering even more impact. Learn more here: UpEnergy Group Why This Role As Carbon Data & QC Ops grows in scale and complexity — more markets, more monthly cycles, more deliverables going to field teams, leadership, auditors and registries — quality and consistency checks need a dedicated owner. This role builds that layer: a second pair of eyes across the team's output before it ships, so reliability doesn't depend on one person catching everything alone. The role starts high-level — general quality assurance across data, forms, reports and tools. As trust and familiarity build, scope naturally grows into broader day-to-day operational support. Role Summary Own quality assurance across the team's deliverables — data, forms, reports, dashboards, and working tools — catching errors early and keeping output reliable and consistent before it goes out. Key Responsibilities Quality review: check deliverables — data outputs, forms, reports, dashboards — for accuracy and consistency before they ship. Source verification: spot-check numbers and records against source data. Review logging: keep a simple, current log of what was checked and what was found — no review without a record. Early escalation: flag anything uncertain the same day rather than guess or sit on it. Day-to-day support: pick up broader operational and data tasks as capacity and trust grow — this role is designed to expand, not stay fixed. Candidate Profile Must-Haves High attention to detail; methodical and comfortable with repetitive, precision-dependent work. Clear written communication — much of the work is asynchronous review and reporting. Proactive problem-solver — surfaces issues with a proposed fix, not just a flag. Reliable and self-directed; this role runs on a checklist and a log, not close supervision. Nice-to-Haves (bonus, not gating) Familiarity with survey/data-collection tools (e.g. XLSForm, SurveyCTO, ODK, KoboToolbox). Basic SQL and/or Python — enough to spot-check a query or re-run a script and read its output. Prior exposure to carbon markets, M&E, or program data — shortens ramp-up, not required. Explicitly Not Required Not a developer hire — no new feature-building or software-engineering expected. No prior carbon-credit or MRV expertise required. What You'll Gain Direct, hands-on mentorship from the Senior Data Analyst on real carbon-market data and operations — not shadow work, actual production deliverables. Broad exposure across data, forms, reporting and tooling — a strong general foundation, not a narrow niche. Growing ownership — the role expands as trust builds, not a role capped at one task forever. A structured ramp-up with regular feedback, not thrown in blind. Decision Rights Tier What it covers Flags & logs — no ask needed Any discrepancy found during review, however small. Decides independently Obvious fixes (typos, formatting); re-running a check after correcting an input error. Never their call What ships externally; final sign-off on anything going to leadership, auditors or registries — that stays with Shoaib. Success — First 90 Days Deliverables going out to field teams or leadership have an independent check behind them. A current, complete review log exists and reflects real work — no gaps. The role has picked up at least one recurring day-to-day task beyond pure review. Practical Details Reports to: Shoaib Ahmed Noorani, Senior Data Analyst, Carbon Data & QC Ops. Engagement: Full-time preferred; initial 3-month trial with extension based on performance. Location: In Office (Bangalore) Why Join Us? Not your average 9-to-5 UpEnergy encourages teamwork, creativity, and we’re not afraid to get our hands dirty. We stay close to our market, understand our customers, and have a lot of fun while doing our work! If you’re looking for a conventional 9-to-5, you’d be missing out on our adventures! Opportunity to do things in a new way As one of the largest compliance credit issuer in Africa, we need to be constantly improving and rethinking our way of work. This means endless opportunities for a self-starter to initiate new ways of doing things or experimenting ways to help us improve. Personal and Career Growth Wouldn’t it be a pity to spend so much time working but not growing and learning? At UpEnergy we value both personal and professional growth, and we want to grow as a team. From classroom training to coffee chats to performance review, we want to support every team member to grow into the best version they can. Create Lasting Impact Our clean energy products bring positive impact to both our planet earth and for the low-income communities we work in. We don’t just focus on sales – we follow up and truly understand our customers to make sure that they continue to benefit from our products. Your work will create much longer-lasting impact than what you can see! Compensation: The Intern will receive a stipend. Internship Duration: 6 months Start date & Location: The position is based in Chennai, India. We are looking for the right candidate to start as soon as possible.

Participate in daily stand-up calls and plan / execute book of work in-line with agile practices. Write unit-test cases and ensure adherence to CICD pipeline criterion to meet quality gates Onboard components on source code repository like Bitbucket/ GitHub and CICD pipeline configurations. Perform application sanity and validation in Canary environments and push to UAT and production Support QA, performance and VA testing for the application by supporting analysis and fixing of any issues identified. Use monitoring tools such as Splunk, AppDynamics to perform the same Optimizing, performance, quality & responsiveness of the Web/Micro services Provide support to running production environment for any issues identified in the applications. Operate with autonomy, while some oversight and direction may be required. Adhere to internal safe coding practices and any other compliance procedures Actively participate in the training process to improve your skills, knowledge of software & Citi applications Expected to provide sound understanding of application development concepts and principles and a basic knowledge of concepts and principles in other technology areas. title: QA Engineer (WFO) - Chennai
description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright · TypeScript · pytest · Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · SQL · REST · OpenAPI · GitHub Actions · Docker · HL7 v2 · FHIR · ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language , enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team Good to have as well Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence Testing integrations with devices or external systems — an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed Security testing basics — role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten — and reading a VAPT report What You'll Bring Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work Methodical about the awkward cases — the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice — because those are where a hospital gets hurt Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover

title: QA Analyst - Intern
description: Job Description: Intern: QA Analyst About Us: UpEnergy is the leading developer of anti-poverty climate impact projects in Africa. We accelerate decarbonization and while delivering long-term health and income benefits in local communities. We provide life-improving clean technologies and carbon reduction and capture projects that protect the local environment, deliver health benefits and cleaner air, and reduce poverty through financial savings and employment. Our project sustainably benefits and enables people to live better lives within more climate resilient communities. To date, UpEnergy has built over 95 emission reduction projects, impacted over 4 million lives, and reduced over 3 million tons of CO2 Emissions across 10 countries. All UpEnergy’s work is characterized by respect for the people we serve, rigorous measurement, deep local knowledge and established teams on the ground to ensure the highest impact and results. We do all this through our commitment to drive long-term business growth through technical innovation, close customer engagement and increased data-driven decision making. The UpEnergy team continues to grow, across multiple African countries, from 20 to over 170+ full time team members in the past two years, reflecting the growth of the company for which we now seek incredible, like-minded talent who are excited to join us in delivering even more impact. Learn more here: UpEnergy Group Why This Role As Carbon Data & QC Ops grows in scale and complexity — more markets, more monthly cycles, more deliverables going to field teams, leadership, auditors and registries — quality and consistency checks need a dedicated owner. This role builds that layer: a second pair of eyes across the team's output before it ships, so reliability doesn't depend on one person catching everything alone. The role starts high-level — general quality assurance across data, forms, reports and tools. As trust and familiarity build, scope naturally grows into broader day-to-day operational support. Role Summary Own quality assurance across the team's deliverables — data, forms, reports, dashboards, and working tools — catching errors early and keeping output reliable and consistent before it goes out. Key Responsibilities Quality review: check deliverables — data outputs, forms, reports, dashboards — for accuracy and consistency before they ship. Source verification: spot-check numbers and records against source data. Review logging: keep a simple, current log of what was checked and what was found — no review without a record. Early escalation: flag anything uncertain the same day rather than guess or sit on it. Day-to-day support: pick up broader operational and data tasks as capacity and trust grow — this role is designed to expand, not stay fixed. Candidate Profile Must-Haves High attention to detail; methodical and comfortable with repetitive, precision-dependent work. Clear written communication — much of the work is asynchronous review and reporting. Proactive problem-solver — surfaces issues with a proposed fix, not just a flag. Reliable and self-directed; this role runs on a checklist and a log, not close supervision. Nice-to-Haves (bonus, not gating) Familiarity with survey/data-collection tools (e.g. XLSForm, SurveyCTO, ODK, KoboToolbox). Basic SQL and/or Python — enough to spot-check a query or re-run a script and read its output. Prior exposure to carbon markets, M&E, or program data — shortens ramp-up, not required. Explicitly Not Required Not a developer hire — no new feature-building or software-engineering expected. No prior carbon-credit or MRV expertise required. What You'll Gain Direct, hands-on mentorship from the Senior Data Analyst on real carbon-market data and operations — not shadow work, actual production deliverables. Broad exposure across data, forms, reporting and tooling — a strong general foundation, not a narrow niche. Growing ownership — the role expands as trust builds, not a role capped at one task forever. A structured ramp-up with regular feedback, not thrown in blind. Decision Rights Tier What it covers Flags & logs — no ask needed Any discrepancy found during review, however small. Decides independently Obvious fixes (typos, formatting); re-running a check after correcting an input error. Never their call What ships externally; final sign-off on anything going to leadership, auditors or registries — that stays with Shoaib. Success — First 90 Days Deliverables going out to field teams or leadership have an independent check behind them. A current, complete review log exists and reflects real work — no gaps. The role has picked up at least one recurring day-to-day task beyond pure review. Practical Details Reports to: Shoaib Ahmed Noorani, Senior Data Analyst, Carbon Data & QC Ops. Engagement: Full-time preferred; initial 3-month trial with extension based on performance. Location: In Office (Bangalore) Why Join Us? Not your average 9-to-5 UpEnergy encourages teamwork, creativity, and we’re not afraid to get our hands dirty. We stay close to our market, understand our customers, and have a lot of fun while doing our work! If you’re looking for a conventional 9-to-5, you’d be missing out on our adventures! Opportunity to do things in a new way As one of the largest compliance credit issuer in Africa, we need to be constantly improving and rethinking our way of work. This means endless opportunities for a self-starter to initiate new ways of doing things or experimenting ways to help us improve. Personal and Career Growth Wouldn’t it be a pity to spend so much time working but not growing and learning? At UpEnergy we value both personal and professional growth, and we want to grow as a team. From classroom training to coffee chats to performance review, we want to support every team member to grow into the best version they can. Create Lasting Impact Our clean energy products bring positive impact to both our planet earth and for the low-income communities we work in. We don’t just focus on sales – we follow up and truly understand our customers to make sure that they continue to benefit from our products. Your work will create much longer-lasting impact than what you can see! Compensation: The Intern will receive a stipend. Internship Duration: 6 months Start date & Location: The position is based in Chennai, India. We are looking for the right candidate to start as soon as possible.

description: Business Analyst II Are you a strategic planner and problem-solver? Are you looking to develop your Data Analyst career? Its capabilities span registration, purchasing, badging and onsite access, connecting customer experiences with the data and business systems behind them. We work across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Product Success and regional business teams to deliver reliable services, improve customer experiences and create measurable business value. About the Role We’re seeking a Business Analyst with a strong focus on User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to bridge product delivery and business validation. You’ll coordinate testing, help business users evaluate new features, manage feedback, and communicate releases in clear, accessible language. The focus is hands-on business acceptance and coordination—not software development or test automation engineering. Responsibilities (What you’ll do) Plan and coordinate business acceptance testing Partner with Product Managers, Product Owners, and Business Analysts to understand desired outcomes, user journeys, business rules, and acceptance criteria. Turn requirements into practical, risk-based UAT scenarios covering standard journeys, exceptions, and relevant regional variations. Coordinate testing scope and schedules, providing participants with clear instructions, test-event links, and prerequisites. Work with engineering, QA, and configuration teams to ensure environments, test data, and configurations are ready before testing. Perform hands-on business validation and help users investigate and reproduce unexpected results. Manage feedback, defects, and acceptance evidence Maintain a consolidated record of business feedback and communicate test completion, outstanding observations, and potential enhancements. Separate defects from configuration issues, clarification requests, and enhancement ideas, working with product and technical teams to agree next steps. Document reproducible issues, including expected and actual results, supporting evidence, and business impact, and coordinate retesting after fixes. Report progress, coverage, blockers, and residual risks so decision-makers can clearly assess readiness. Coordinate acceptance evidence and follow-up while keeping approval and validation accountability with the relevant Business Units. Support release communication and continuous improvement Prepare business-facing release updates that explain what changed, why it matters, and any relevant limitations or actions. Keep testing guidance, feedback records, and supporting documentation accessible to global stakeholders. Create reusable scenarios and checklists to improve consistency and reduce repeated effort across releases. Apply lessons from UAT and production issues to strengthen future acceptance coverage and identify gaps earlier. Collaborate across regions and time zones, keeping dependencies, decisions, and ownership clear. Requirements (What you’ll bring) Practical experience in UAT, business analysis, functional testing, or a similar role supporting user-facing digital products. Experience translating requirements and business processes into clear acceptance criteria and end-to-end test scenarios. Ability to organize testing with business users, balance competing priorities, and follow issues through to documented outcomes. Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to explain business impact as well as technical symptoms. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing user guidance, test summaries, and release updates. Experience with issue-tracking and collaborative documentation tools such as Jira and Confluence, or equivalents. Understanding of Agile delivery and the differences between engineering QA, business acceptance, and release approval. A collaborative approach and confidence working with technical and non-technical stakeholders in a distributed team. Useful, but not essential, skills Experience with event registration, ticketing, eCommerce, or other transaction-based customer journeys. Familiarity with payments, invoicing, discounts, upgrades, entitlements, or integrations between customer-facing and back-office systems. Exposure to onsite operational tools, badge management, or access-control workflows. Awareness of accessibility, localization, and data-quality considerations in business acceptance testing. Experience with test-management tools, basic data queries, or API-testing tools to support investigations. What success looks like Business users know what to test, how to participate, and where to provide feedback. Critical business journeys have clear acceptance coverage and traceable results. Defects and feedback are actionable, assigned, and followed through, with unresolved risks visible before release decisions. Business approvers receive concise evidence to support acceptance decisions. Release communications clearly explain changes and limitations, helping teams prepare for adoption. Reusable guidance and lessons learned make each testing cycle more effective. Why join us? Help shape digital experiences that connect online registration with the live event experience. description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright · TypeScript · pytest · Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · SQL · REST · OpenAPI · GitHub Actions · Docker · HL7 v2 · FHIR · ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language , enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team Good to have as well Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence Testing integrations with devices or external systems — an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed Security testing basics — role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten — and reading a VAPT report What You'll Bring Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work Methodical about the awkward cases — the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice — because those are where a hospital gets hurt Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover

title: Business Analyst II
description: Are you a strategic planner and problem-solver? Are you looking to develop your Data Analyst career? About The Team Mercury is RX’s global registration and eCommerce platform, supporting the journeys that bring visitors and exhibitors into our events. Its capabilities span registration, purchasing, badging and onsite access, connecting customer experiences with the data and business systems behind them. We work across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Product Success and regional business teams to deliver reliable services, improve customer experiences and create measurable business value. About The Role We’re seeking a Business Analyst with a strong focus on User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to bridge product delivery and business validation. You’ll coordinate testing, help business users evaluate new features, manage feedback, and communicate releases in clear, accessible language. The focus is hands-on business acceptance and coordination—not software development or test automation engineering. Responsibilities (What You’ll Do) Plan and coordinate business acceptance testing Partner with Product Managers, Product Owners, and Business Analysts to understand desired outcomes, user journeys, business rules, and acceptance criteria. Turn requirements into practical, risk-based UAT scenarios covering standard journeys, exceptions, and relevant regional variations. Coordinate testing scope and schedules, providing participants with clear instructions, test-event links, and prerequisites. Work with engineering, QA, and configuration teams to ensure environments, test data, and configurations are ready before testing. Perform hands-on business validation and help users investigate and reproduce unexpected results. Manage feedback, defects, and acceptance evidence Maintain a consolidated record of business feedback and communicate test completion, outstanding observations, and potential enhancements. Separate defects from configuration issues, clarification requests, and enhancement ideas, working with product and technical teams to agree next steps. Document reproducible issues, including expected and actual results, supporting evidence, and business impact, and coordinate retesting after fixes. Report progress, coverage, blockers, and residual risks so decision-makers can clearly assess readiness. Coordinate acceptance evidence and follow-up while keeping approval and validation accountability with the relevant Business Units. Support release communication and continuous improvement Prepare business-facing release updates that explain what changed, why it matters, and any relevant limitations or actions. Keep testing guidance, feedback records, and supporting documentation accessible to global stakeholders. Create reusable scenarios and checklists to improve consistency and reduce repeated effort across releases. Apply lessons from UAT and production issues to strengthen future acceptance coverage and identify gaps earlier. Collaborate across regions and time zones, keeping dependencies, decisions, and ownership clear. Requirements (What You’ll Bring) Practical experience in UAT, business analysis, functional testing, or a similar role supporting user-facing digital products. Experience translating requirements and business processes into clear acceptance criteria and end-to-end test scenarios. Ability to organize testing with business users, balance competing priorities, and follow issues through to documented outcomes. Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to explain business impact as well as technical symptoms. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing user guidance, test summaries, and release updates. Experience with issue-tracking and collaborative documentation tools such as Jira and Confluence, or equivalents. Understanding of Agile delivery and the differences between engineering QA, business acceptance, and release approval. A collaborative approach and confidence working with technical and non-technical stakeholders in a distributed team. Useful, But Not Essential, Skills Experience with event registration, ticketing, eCommerce, or other transaction-based customer journeys. Familiarity with payments, invoicing, discounts, upgrades, entitlements, or integrations between customer-facing and back-office systems. Exposure to onsite operational tools, badge management, or access-control workflows. Awareness of accessibility, localization, and data-quality considerations in business acceptance testing. Experience with test-management tools, basic data queries, or API-testing tools to support investigations. What Success Looks Like Business users know what to test, how to participate, and where to provide feedback. Critical business journeys have clear acceptance coverage and traceable results. Defects and feedback are actionable, assigned, and followed through, with unresolved risks visible before release decisions. Business approvers receive concise evidence to support acceptance decisions. Release communications clearly explain changes and limitations, helping teams prepare for adoption. Reusable guidance and lessons learned make each testing cycle more effective. Why join us? Help shape digital experiences that connect online registration with the live event experience. You’ll work across product, technology, and business operations, building domain knowledge while improving how changes are validated and communicated. RX values collaboration, inclusion, curiosity, and learning, with opportunities to contribute across a global network. Work in a Way That Works for You We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organization. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous well-being initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals. Working for You Benefits We know that your wellbeing and happiness are key to a long and successful career. These are some of the benefits we are delighted to offer: Comprehensive Health Insurance: Covers you, your immediate family, and parents Enhanced Health Insurance Options: Competitive rates negotiated by the company Group Life Insurance: Ensuring financial security for your loved ones Group Accident Insurance: Extra protection for accidental death and permanent disablement Flexible Working Arrangement: Achieve a harmonious work-life balance Employee Assistance Program: Access support for personal and work-related challenges Medical Screening: Your well-being is a top priority Modern Family Benefits: Maternity, paternity, and adoption support Long-Service Awards: Recognizing dedication and commitment New Baby Gift: Celebrating the joy of parenthood Subsidized Meals in Chennai: Enjoy delicious meals at discounted rates Various Paid Time Off: Take time off with Casual Leave, Sick Leave, Privilege Leave, Compassionate Leave, Special Sick Leave, and Gazetted Public Holidays About The Business RX is a global leader in events and exhibitions, leveraging industry expertise, data, and technology to build businesses for individuals, communities, and organizations. With a presence in 25 countries across 41 industry sectors, RX hosts approximately 350 events annually. RX is committed to creating an inclusive work environment for all our people. RX empowers businesses to thrive by leveraging data-driven insights and digital solutions. RX is part of RELX, a global provider of information-based analytics and decision tools for professional and business customers.
